subject: crabeater seal
title: Four in Five Crabeater Seals Wear the Same Scars

scenes.text: Four out of five adult crabeater seals carry the same scars.
Long parallel gashes along their sides and back flippers, as if raked by a giant comb.
And despite the name, crabs have nothing to do with it. They eat almost nothing but krill.
The marks are teeth. They come from the crabeater's main hunter, the leopard seal.
Most attacks hit pups in their first year, and many never reach their second.
So every scarred adult on the ice is one that got away.

description:
Studies in the Antarctic found that around 80% of adult crabeater seals carry scars from leopard seal attacks, most picked up as pups in their first year, when leopard seals kill many of them.
Despite their name, crabeaters live almost entirely on Antarctic krill, which they strain through lobed teeth.
Would you rather be the crabeater or the leopard seal?
first_comment: Bonus: crabeaters are thought to be the most numerous seal on Earth, numbering in the millions. Which predator would you least want to meet on the ice?
